reason: Conversation 2 correctly identified the RCD from 'half the house' going off, laid out plausible causes with the fan element first, asked efficient questions, used the grill result to honestly narrow to the fan element or motor (with an appropriate caveat that one test isn't conclusive), and escalated to an engineer with insulation testing while keeping the part recommendation conditional. Conversation 1 reached the right safety instruction but overstated the danger, told the homeowner to 'unplug' a hardwired built-in, offered no diagnosis beyond a guess, asked nothing, and ended the conversation. Conversation 2's weaknesses are real but minor: it invited removing the fan cover and running further defrost/grill tests on an appliance that is leaking to earth, and left the grill in use with a 'keep an eye on it' rather than isolating fully, which drifts toward the 'safe to keep using the grill' unsupported claim.
